candidates.title: DP World expands crane capacity at London Gateway and Southampton
candidates.excerpt: DP World is expanding container handling capacity at its UK terminals with the arrival of new quay cranes at London Gateway and Southampton. Two cranes have arrived fully assembled at London Gateway following a journey from Shanghai. Each weighs more than 2,000 tonnes and stands nearly 150 metres high. The cranes will be installed at the new all-electric Berth 5, which is currently under construction as part of DP World’s £1 billion expansion of London Gateway. The berth is scheduled to become operational in 2027. A further two cranes are expected to arrive at Southampton next week. They follow the delivery of two cranes to the terminal in June, bringing the total number of quay cranes serving Southampton to 16. New cranes designed for 24,000 TEU ships The four cranes delivered to Southampton during 2026 represent an investment of £60 million. candidates.title: Boluda Towage adds new tug to La Réunion fleet
candidates.excerpt: Boluda Towage has expanded its fleet in La Réunion with the deployment of the new tug VB Audace. The Damen ASD 2811 vessel entered service at the Port of Le Port in mid-September. Damen Song Cam built the tug in 2026. VB Audace has an engine output of 5,102 hp and a bollard pull of 60 tonnes. These specifications allow the vessel to perform a range of harbour towage operations. The tug completed its first assignments shortly after arriving on the island. “VB Audace will strengthen and complete the fleet in service for the port,” said Christophe C. P. Picard, Managing Director of Boluda La Réunion. Boluda Towage said the deployment will increase its capacity to support growing maritime traffic and port operations in La Réunion.

Erasmus Shipinvest also ordered two 1,800 TEU containerships earlier in 2026. As a result, the company now has eight firm containerships on order at Huangpu Wenchong, along with options for another six vessels.

Rhenus is also working with Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ), the country’s national railway company, on capacity development along the corridor. Under the current project design, the facility is expected to add at least 150,000 TEU of annual handling capacity at Aktau. candidates.title: Friends of East Broad Top raises $564,516, opens 2027 campaign
candidates.excerpt: SALTILLO, Pa. – Friends of the East Broad Top Railroad officers announced on Thursday, Oct. 1, that the group had raised a record $564,516 from 1,456 donors in its 2026 campaign, and kicked off an equally ambitious fundraising drive for 2027. The nonprofit organization is the all-volunteer auxiliary to the EBT Foundation, Inc., which owns the East Broad Top Railroad, a narrow-gauge heritage line in central Pennsylvania that is a National Historic Landmark. For its 2027 campaign, which began Thursday, the Friends set a goal of $375,000. The single largest chunk of that is earmarked for the two groups’ drive to continue to open 9 miles of main line – idled for 70 years – linking EBT headquarters at Rockhill Furnace, Pa., and the town of Saltillo. candidates.title: ONE folds Hong Kong regional HQ into Singapore
candidates.excerpt: Ocean Network Express is consolidating its Asian regional management in Singapore, folding its Hong Kong-based East Asia headquarters into a new Asia Pacific operation from April 1, 2027. The Japanese containerline said the new Asia Pacific regional headquarters will combine its current East Asia operation in Hong Kong with the South Asia headquarters already based in Singapore. The enlarged unit will oversee 15 markets, with Louis Tang appointed regional head. ONE is also redrawing responsibility for Africa. Its East, West and South African businesses will move under the carrier’s Dubai regional headquarters, while London will retain responsibility for Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa. The restructuring alters a regional setup that dates back to ONE’s creation. When NYK, MOL and K Line unveiled their merged container operation in 2017, Singapore was selected as global headquarters, with regional headquarters initially established in Hong Kong, London, Richmond and São Paulo.

Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. The 20-year-old, 2,490 teu MSC Hermes III was reported to have sent a distress call at around 08:45 hrs SGT on 22 September and was rebroadcast by Singapore MRCC according to the Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore (MPA). The 25 crew of the vessel were reported to have abandoned ship into a lifeboat and were rescued by another MSC vessel MSC Ruby which answered the distress call. Two other MSC vessels MSC Florentina and the MSC Turin III also diverted to the vicinity of the MSC Hermes III that appeared to be adrift around 300 km east of Vietnam. candidates.title: Triple newbuild joy for fast expanding RCL
candidates.excerpt: Triple newbuild joy for fast expanding RCL Regional Container Lines has named a trio of newbuildings in China as the company grows its capacity 157% in coming years Bangkok-headquartered Regional Container Lines (RCL) has named three new 4,488 teu newbuildings at CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding in China. The Annita Bhum, Benyapar Bhum, and Chantisa Bhum were named at the shipbuilders Longxue Yard in Guangzhou on 24 September. The naming ceremony was attended by RCL’s senior leadership, Dr. Jamlong Atikul, Chairman of the Board of Directors, Sumate Tanthuwanit, Chairman of the Executive Committee of RCL, and Dr. Twinchok Tanthuwanit, President of RCL, along with industry guests and stakeholders. The three newbuilds are the first in a series of eight container ships being built by RCL at CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. Burglary hits moving BNSF train as container catches fire in Riverside
candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east.
